plants.name: Euphorbia pulcherrima
plants.description: A shrub with showy colored bracts surrounding small yellow flower clusters called cyathia. In its native Mexico it grows into a shrub up to 4 meters tall, and in frost-free regions it is a common landscape plant. Elsewhere it is grown as a potted holiday plant.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late autumn to winter (November to February)
plants.location: Native to southern Mexico and Central America; cultivated worldwide
plants.funFact: The colorful 'petals' are actually modified leaves called bracts, and the plant needs long nights of about 12 hours of darkness for several weeks to develop its color.

plants.name: Helleborus niger
plants.description: An evergreen perennial with nodding, cup-shaped white flowers with golden-yellow stamens that fade to pink as they age. It thrives in partial shade and cool, humus-rich soil, and blooms when little else does in the garden.
plants.bloomingSeason: Early winter to early spring (December to March)
plants.location: Mountain woodlands of central and southern Europe, including the Alps and northern Apennines; cultivated in temperate gardens worldwide
plants.funFact: Despite its name it is not a rose but a member of the buttercup family, and all parts of the plant are poisonous.

plants.name: Delonix regia
plants.description: A spreading tree with a wide umbrella-shaped canopy and fern-like leaves. In the Southern Hemisphere summer it becomes covered in clusters of vivid orange-red flowers, each with a distinctive spotted upper petal. It is widely planted as a street and shade tree in the tropics and subtropics.
plants.bloomingSeason: Summer in the Southern Hemisphere (November to January); May to July in the Northern Hemisphere tropics
plants.location: Native to Madagascar; widely cultivated in tropical regions including northern Australia, Brazil, and southern Africa
plants.funFact: It is endangered in its native Madagascar, yet it is one of the most widely planted ornamental trees in the world.

plants.name: Camellia japonica
plants.description: An evergreen shrub or small tree with glossy dark green leaves and large, rose-like flowers. It prospers in mild, humid climates and blooms through the cool season, brightening winter gardens when most plants are dormant.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late autumn to early spring (December to April)
plants.location: Native to Japan, Korea, and eastern China; cultivated in the southeastern United States, Europe, Australia, and New Zealand
plants.funFact: Camellia japonica is the official flower of Alabama, and there are thousands of cultivars; in Japan it is known as tsubaki and has been celebrated for centuries.
